Four years after the death of a young woman whose name became synonymous with the fight for women's rights and freedom in Iran, Amnesty International says the resulting government crackdown was a systemic campaign whose perpetrators continue to evade accountability.

Mahsa Amini was 22 when she died on Sept. 16, 2022, after being arrested by Iran's morality police for "unsuitable attire."

Wednesday's Amnesty report — a mammoth undertaking drawing on 270 interviews, more than 2,000 videos and extensive documentary evidence — says those same officials continue to lead violent crackdowns now. It identifies dozens of officials allegedly responsible for committing what it describes as crimes against humanity.

Georgia and Texas had each planned to put a man to death within an hour of each other on Wednesday before a court stepped in to halt the one in Georgia for now, while Alabama is set to carry out another execution the following day.

Texas remains scheduled to execute LeJames Norman on Wednesday after a Georgia judge stayed Stacey Humphreys’ execution late Tuesday.

In the Peach State, 53-year-old Stacey Humphreys was set to be executed on Wednesday for his conviction in the 2003 murders of two real estate agents, 21-year-old Lori Brown and 33-year-old Cindy Williams.

But a Cobb County judge stayed his execution late Tuesday, meaning the execution cannot move forward unless the stay is lifted or overturned by a higher court.
